newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK activists fined for storming of Japan consulate.
newsitem.headline: HK activists fined for storming of Japan consulate.

text.p: Three Hong Kong activists were convicted on Monday of unlawful assembly and fined HK$4,000 (US$516) each for storming Japan's consulate in the territory last year to protest Tokyo's claims to a disputed island chain.
Court officials said four other protesters were acquitted at the hearing in a local court.
One of those convicted over last October's incident was Lo Chiu-fai, a member of a pro-democracy political group called The Frontier.
The convictions coincide with fresh protests over the disputed Diaoyu islands in the East China Sea after a Japanese rightist group landed on one of the isles last Tuesday.
Japan, China and Taiwan all claim ownership of the islands, known as Diaoyu in China and Senkaku in Japan.
On Sunday, about 100 people took to the streets in Hong Kong to protest the landing by a group led by Japanese legislator Shingo Nishimura.
Protests last year were sparked when a Japanese rightest group erected a lighthouse on one of the islands in July.
The issue of sovereignty over the islands has lit nationalistic passions in Chinese communities in Hong Kong and Taiwan.
Activists from Hong Kong and Taiwan plan to sail to the Japanese-administered islands, rocky outcrops lying between Taiwan and Japan's Okinawa island chain, on May 18 to "reclaim" them.
In September, a Hong Kong activist drowned when he jumped into stormy waters near the islands to press China's claim.
